5 things that only happen in Bali ✨ Save this for your trip.

05 Everyone's called Wayan, Made, Nyoman or Ketut (it's birth order)
04 Rice terraces share water through 1,000-year-old temple networks
03 Every 210 days, bamboo penjor line the streets for Galungan
02 People sleep with their heads towards the mountain
01 An orchestra of voices, no instruments, on a clifftop at sunset

Number 1 is the Kecak at Uluwatu, a short drive from Yume by Nyara: three private-pool villas above Bingin. Link in bio to book your stay in Bali.

slides.sub: Number 1 happens every evening, a short drive from our villas.

slides.answer: It's your place in the family.
slides.body: First-borns are Wayan (or Putu, Gede), then come Made, Nyoman and Ketut. Child number five? Wayan Balik: “Wayan again”.
Bali's rice terraces run on subak, a farmer-led water system dating back to the 9th century. Water temples guide it, and UNESCO listed the landscape in 2012.

slides.img: commons:File:Penjors lining a public street in Bali.jpg
slides.body: Bali runs on its own 210-day calendar. Each cycle, families raise tall, decorated penjor for Galungan, ten days of celebration. The next one starts on 13 January 2027.
Balinese life is oriented around the mountains, above all Mount Agung. Family temples sit on the mountain side, and people sleep with their heads facing that way, called kaja.
Every evening around 6pm, a circle of men chants the Kecak on a clifftop beside Uluwatu Temple, telling the Ramayana as the sun goes down. It's a short drive from Yume.

slides.credit: Villa Tiga, Yume by Nyara, Bingin
slides.body: Three private-pool villas on the clifftops of Bingin, four minutes on foot from Impossible Beach. From USD 135 a night.
